messages.author: Callum Reid
messages.text:
Hey,
Proposing the carrier-feed resource hierarchy should be
```Carrier
 ├── Account 1
 │    ├── Depot A
 │    │   ├── Shipment i
 │    │   ├── Shipment ii
 │    └── Depot B
 ├── Account 2
 ...```
<@W5EXAMPLEHANA|Hana Mori> your docs suggested we have the charge type underneath shipment but that doesn't make any sense from the EDI 210 docs. Though we aren't going to be compliant with the full standard, if we are trying to follow it we should follow it:
>  _"Resource: A unique component that incurs a charge" -_ EDI 210 implementation guide, glossary
and
> _"Service: An offering that can be purchased from a carrier, and can include many types of charges; e.g., a linehaul service may include fuel, tolls, and detention charges" -_ EDI 210 implementation guide, glossary
The charge types themselves are not components that are incurring charges, it is the shipments. The service is the offering we are purchasing through that component, which in this case would be the charge type.

There is example data in "QA Lane Driven" in sit to inspect and more info in <https://northwindlogistics.atlassian.net/wiki/x/KQ7mTA|northwindlogistics.atlassian.net/wiki/x/KQ7mTA>

messages.author: Priya Kanth
messages.text:
<@W5EXAMPLEHANA|Hana Mori> there's a bit of a further level of complexity here, because we can't really get `Depot > Shipment` level granularity out of the parcel feed. So there's not going to be a consistent hierarchy.

There's a useful table on LaneLens' website <https://docs.lanelens.example/managed-freight-tags#supported-carriers|here> which outlines which carriers provide which details, as LaneLens has a concept of "Managed Freight Tags" which aligns closely with our unified EDI 210 hierarchy we're trying to build.

Haulytics also has a similar acknowledgement <https://docs.haulytics.example/user-guide/virtual-tags/canonical-freight-taxonomy|here>:

messages.author: Priya Kanth
Hana Mori
messages.text:
Generally agree.
So basically, that means for the parcel feed, we should have hub as Resource, fuel-surcharge-zone-4 (description from cost) should be EDI 210 (cost and usage). Sounds right to me.

Highlight of coming release (NOT FINAL)
For the full list, please visit <https://northwindlogistics.atlassian.net/issues/?filter=12418|northwindlogistics.atlassian.net/issues?filter=12418>

:ledger: *Configurable Standard GL*
_The Standard GL was a rigid, fixed-format export that customers reformatted by hand every month. Sign presentation and per-account files landed last release; this one adds on-screen review, renamed column headers and the configurable clearing line._
• *Review and Export Standard GL*
    ◦ The General Ledger can now be reviewed on screen before export, with quick filters, a *View By* breakdown and reorderable columns.
• *Configure Standard GL Column Headers*
    ◦ Portal admins can rename Standard GL column headers so the export matches their ERP and internal accounting terminology, without changing the underlying data.
• *Configure Clearing Line*
    ◦ Admins can configure how clearing lines are generated, so the export aligns with their accounting and reconciliation requirements. Clearing lines appear in the export only.
• *Link New Charges to Standard GL*
    ◦ *New Charge* columns on the bill now link through to the *General Ledger*, carrying the report month and billing account across.
• *Group and Sort GL Entries*
    ◦ GL entries are now sorted by billing account and invoice number before any other sorting is applied.
:page_with_curl: *Kowhai Customised GL*
_Kowhai's GL codes run across Depot, Project and Analysis segments, and one lane's cost is charged back over several cost centres, which the standard GL cannot express. The epic's only story so far lands this release._
• *Kowhai Customised GL* :large_yellow_circle: _In QA_
    ◦ A SAP GL upload file runs per billing account and report month, driven by cost centre allocation, with a header block and clearing rows.
:card_index_dividers: *Shipment, Vehicle and Driver Profiles*
_The Shipment, Vehicle and Driver profiles are hard to scan, with poor layout, excess white space and fields that carry nothing for the record in front of the reader. All three are regrouped this release; telematics fields follow._
• *Shipment and Vehicle Overview Tabs in Cards* :large_yellow_circle: _In QA_
    ◦ The Shipment and Vehicle Overview tabs now present their properties in cards laid out four to a row, rather than one long list.
• *Driver Overview Tab in Cards* :large_orange_circle: _In Review_
    ◦ The Driver Overview tab now leads with what kind of record it is, grouping properties into *Details*, *Custom Fields* and *Cost Centre* cards.
• *Empty States on the Driver Profile* :large_yellow_circle: _In QA_
    ◦ Where a tenant has configured no custom fields, the card stays in place and offers a *Configure custom fields* button rather than looking broken.
:truck: *Cost Insights*
_Cost Insights is in beta and the epic has been steadily refining its reporting, with the dashboard widgets and beta landing page last release. This release tidies the cost tables and names the cost basis in exports._
• *Cost Basis in Export Filenames*
    ◦ Cost Insights report exports now carry the cost basis, *EffectiveCost* or *BilledCost*, in the filename, so the basis is clear without opening the file.
• *Truncated Lane Names in Cost Tables*
    ◦ Long lane names in the lane cost tables are truncated with an ellipsis and a hover tooltip, so table layout stays consistent.
:bar_chart: *Report and Listing Changes*
• *Very Small Weights in Reports*
    ◦ Weights below 0.01 kg no longer display as zero, so on-screen figures match the weights shown in exports.
• *Whitespace-insensitive Consignment Number Search*
    ◦ Consignment number searches now match whether or not spaces are typed, so a consignment is found without knowing how its number is stored.
• *Portal User in the Imported By Column*
    ◦ The Import listing *Imported By* column now shows the Portal User rather than an email address, in both the customer and admin portals.
:gear: *Admin Console / Operation Change*
• *Billing Accounts Moved to Portal Settings*
    ◦ The *Billing Accounts* menu item has moved from Settings to Portal Settings, keeping Settings focused on the features admins use most.
• *See All Active Workflows in Admin Console*
    ◦ A new *Workflows* page under Tenants lists every active workflow, on screen and in export, under the existing tenant permission.
• *More Feature Statistics in Admin Console* :large_orange_circle: _In Review_
    ◦ The *Customer Statistic Report* adds adoption figures such as SSO provider and allocation type, on screen and in export.
• *Clearer Error Messages in Admin* :large_yellow_circle: _In QA_
    ◦ Global errors always show additional info, and failed bill processes offer a dialog to read and copy the full message.
• *CCH Custom GL File Update*
    ◦ The Coral Coast Haulage custom GL file drops the *Jnl Preparer* column, so it no longer has to be removed monthly.
• *Migrate Templates*
    ◦ Meridian Rail CT Bill
:smiley: *Misc. UX Improvements*
• *New Logo on the Login Page* :large_yellow_circle: _In QA_
    ◦ The login screen now carries the new Northwind logo, with alignment and spacing updated to match the supplied reference.
*Sent using* <@WEEXAMPLECLDE|Claude>

messages.author: Callum Reid
messages.text:
Hey,
Proposing the carrier-feed resource hierarchy should be
```Carrier
 ├── Account 1
 │    ├── Depot A
 │    │   ├── Shipment i
 │    │   ├── Shipment ii
 │    └── Depot B
 ├── Account 2
 ...```
<@W5EXAMPLEHANA|Hana Mori> your docs suggested we have the charge type underneath shipment but that doesn't make any sense from the EDI 210 docs. Though we aren't going to be compliant with the full standard, if we are trying to follow it we should follow it:
>  _"Resource: A unique component that incurs a charge" -_ EDI 210 implementation guide, glossary
and
> _"Service: An offering that can be purchased from a carrier, and can include many types of charges; e.g., a linehaul service may include fuel, tolls, and detention charges" -_ EDI 210 implementation guide, glossary
The charge types themselves are not components that are incurring charges, it is the shipments. The service is the offering we are purchasing through that component, which in this case would be the charge type.

There is example data in "QA Lane Driven" in sit to inspect and more info in <https://northwindlogistics.atlassian.net/wiki/x/KQ7mTA|northwindlogistics.atlassian.net/wiki/x/KQ7mTA>

messages.author: Priya Kanth
messages.text:
<@W5EXAMPLEHANA|Hana Mori> there's a bit of a further level of complexity here, because we can't really get `Depot > Shipment` level granularity out of the parcel feed. So there's not going to be a consistent hierarchy.

There's a useful table on LaneLens' website <https://docs.lanelens.example/managed-freight-tags#supported-carriers|here> which outlines which carriers provide which details, as LaneLens has a concept of "Managed Freight Tags" which aligns closely with our unified EDI 210 hierarchy we're trying to build.

Haulytics also has a similar acknowledgement <https://docs.haulytics.example/user-guide/virtual-tags/canonical-freight-taxonomy|here>:

messages.author: Priya Kanth
Hana Mori
messages.text:
Generally agree.
So basically, that means for the parcel feed, we should have hub as Resource, fuel-surcharge-zone-4 (description from cost) should be EDI 210 (cost and usage). Sounds right to me.
